title: adaptive-attention-accelerator-adaptor-integration-and-rollout
creator: Sara Kim
description: Integrate a lightweight adaptor layer that can dynamically choose between FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels at runtime based on per-request shape, memory headroom, and SLO targets. The adaptor should expose a deterministic policy, strong telemetry + fallback paths, and a staged rollout plan with automatic rollback on regression signals.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptor is loaded as a pluggable strategy in the attention runtime and can be toggled via config flag
Per-shape decision logic selects v2 or v3 with recorded rationale in traces
No increased incidence of OOMs on our 32GB and 80GB GPU fleets during canary traffic
End-to-end latency P95 for decoder workloads does not regress >2% in canary compared to baseline
Automated golden regression jobs detect functional differences and flag any token-level deltas
Canary rollout automation can rollback the adaptor within 5 minutes of threshold breach
tasks: Design adaptor API and decision inputs (shapes, kv-cache size, workspace availability, requested precision)
Implement kernel selector shim with hooks into existing kernel registry
Add telemetry: decision events, memory headroom snapshot, kernel latency samples per shape
Create golden regression tests (deterministic seeds + representative prompts)
Run large-scale soak tests across 32GB and 80GB fleet images
Create staged rollout plan (local dev -> canary 2% -> canary 10% -> ramp) and automation playbook
Author docs for operator config flags and emergency rollback steps
Land unit + integration tests and submit PR for review
progress_updates: 2025-11-06: Spike complete. Prototype selector implemented as a thin shim that consults a heuristic: sequence length, batch size, and approximate KV cache footprint. Microbench shows v2 wins on short sequences (<=64) with batch sizes up to 8; v3 wins on long sequences (>=512) when memory workspace is available.

2025-11-08: Telemetry schema drafted. Decision events include: chosen_kernel, decision_reason, estimated_workspace_bytes, observed_latency_ms. Added initial trace integration to token-level traces for debugging.

2025-11-10: Ran 6-hour soak on synthetic decoder workload (seq=1024, batch=4) on 80GB machines. Observed 7% p95 improvement with adaptor choosing v3 for long sequences. Noticed transient 1 in 10k OOM when multiple large requests co-locate — root cause likely workspace accounting race in v3 kernel claims.

2025-11-12: Implemented conservative workspace reservation heuristic and retry-with-fallback-on-oom. Reproduced previous OOM locally and verified retry path chooses v2 successfully and request completes. Preparing canary plan.
decisions: Use heuristic-first approach (lightweight, no heavy profiling) for initial rollout to minimize risk
Record decision rationale in traces to allow retrospective analysis and tuning
Implement optimistic v3 selection but fall back to v2 on OOM or workspace acquisition failures
Expose operator override flags to force a single kernel platform per pool for troubleshooting
open_questions: What thresholds should we use for workspace headroom on mixed-tenant machines to avoid noisy neighbors?
Do we need a per-tenant priority bucket to avoid starving latency-critical requests when v3 wants to use large workspace?
Should quantized kernels be treated as a separate partition in the decision graph (i.e., q4/q8 variants)?
risks_mitigations: Risk: v3 workspace allocation can fail under bursty co-location -> Mitigation: conservative reservation + immediate fallback to v2 + alerting on allocation failure rates
Risk: behavioral regressions (token diffs) between v2 and v3 -> Mitigation: golden-regression harness and token-diff thresholds in canary automation
Risk: selector oscillation under mixed workloads -> Mitigation: hysteresis window (sticky decisions for N tokens) and rate limit decision changes per request
Risk: telemetry volume overhead -> Mitigation: sample decision events at 1% for high-traffic routes, full capture for canary buckets
dependencies: ENG-925740 (prefill inference adaptive fallback controller) - for integration with existing fallback hooks
ENG-412358 (attn-cost-gating-and-gradual-compat-rollout) - rollout automation and cost gates
